name: Spatial Vocalizer: metric spatial language vs direct VLM numbers
question: Does converting camera data into an explicit mechanical spatial language (scene graph with metric positions, sizes, confidences) make an LLM arm beat a VLM that reads target coordinates straight off the image?

environment.scenes: 12 synthetic tabletop scenes (4-6 table objects + 1 stacked probe), two pinhole views, baseline 15 cm, metric grid on table
environment.tasks: ~22 commands: right_of (+10cm), front_of (+8cm), midpoint; ground-truth target from a fixed relation table, never from either arm

arms.SL: two-view triangulated scene graph (mechanical) -> LLM parses command to intention {source, relation, refs} with ZERO numbers -> target computed from the same fixed table
arms.Direct: single-view image (grid as scale reference) -> VLM outputs target_xy_m directly

predictions.claim: SL mean error < Direct mean error on paired tasks (one-sided sign-flip permutation p < 0.05); SL error shows no positive trend with scene object count while Direct does (descriptive).
predictions.falsifies: If Direct <= SL or SL error also grows with complexity, the spatial-language layer is not carrying the metric load and the architecture claim fails.

predictions.claim: For the stacked (off-plane) probe: two-view reconstruction keeps xy error < 2 cm and recovers height (z error < 2 cm); single view + table-plane prior collapses (xy error an order of magnitude larger, z error = full host height). Table-level objects: both fine (honest boundary: single view + calibration + plane prior suffices on a plane).
predictions.falsifies: If two-view is not better on off-plane objects, multi-frame calibration is unnecessary in this regime and the multi-view claim is dropped.

predictions.claim: SL intentions contain zero numeric coordinate fields (mechanical check: keys subset of {source, relation, refs}); every SL failure is attributable to wrong_object or geometry_error (100% coverage); Direct failures/misses carry no attribution.
predictions.falsifies: If the render/parsing layer leaks numbers, grounding is broken and P272's architecture does not transfer to the spatial domain.

fairness_notes: Both arms get the same declared coordinate frame and grid scale reference.
Direct gets ONE view (current default); SL needs two views by design -- that cost is part of the claim being tested (P-spatial-2 quantifies what the second view buys).
The relation table is shared: ground truth and SL use the SAME table, so SL has no hidden semantic advantage.
Recognition is solved by construction (unique color+kind); the test isolates metric spatial reasoning.
scoring: euclidean distance of predicted target to ground-truth target (meters), pass <= 3 cm; failures attributed (SL) or recorded raw (Direct)
